_note: Mock flashcards: 6 tagged mistakes, 2 cards each. Every answer is worked in 'explain'. g = 9.8 m/s^2, O = 16.00 g/mol.

cards.prompt: A 2.0 kg block rests on a 30° incline. What is the normal force on it?
cards.explain: N = mg cos θ = 2.0 × 9.8 × cos 30° = 19.6 × 0.866 ≈ 17.0 N. 19.6 N is mg, which ignores the tilt; 9.8 N is mg sin 30°, the part along the slope.

cards.prompt: As the incline gets steeper, what happens to the normal force on the block?
cards.explain: N = mg cos θ, and cos θ falls as θ grows, so N decreases. At 90° the surface is a wall and N = 0.

mistakes.subject: physics
mistakes.title: Sign of g when up is positive

cards.prompt: Up is positive. A ball is thrown straight up at 12 m/s. What is its acceleration while it rises?
cards.explain: Gravity points down and down is negative here, so a = −9.8 m/s² for the whole flight, rising or falling. It is not zero at the top either.

cards.prompt: Up is positive. The same ball, thrown up at 12 m/s: what is its velocity after 2.0 s?
cards.explain: v = v₀ + at = 12 + (−9.8)(2.0) = 12 − 19.6 = −7.6 m/s. The minus sign means it is already falling. +31.6 m/s comes from giving g the wrong sign.

mistakes.subject: chemistry
mistakes.title: Molar mass of a diatomic gas

cards.prompt: What is the molar mass of oxygen gas, O₂? (O = 16.00 g/mol)
cards.explain: Oxygen gas is O₂, two atoms per molecule: 2 × 16.00 = 32.00 g/mol. 16.00 g/mol is a single O atom.

cards.prompt: How many moles are in 8.0 g of O₂?
cards.explain: n = m / M = 8.0 g ÷ 32.00 g/mol = 0.25 mol. 0.50 mol uses 16.00 g/mol (atomic O); 256 multiplies instead of dividing.

cards.prompt: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. How many moles of H₂O form from 3.0 mol of O₂, with H₂ in excess?
cards.explain: The equation gives 2 mol H₂O per 1 mol O₂: 3.0 × 2/1 = 6.0 mol. 3.0 mol assumes 1 : 1; 1.5 mol turns the ratio upside down.

cards.prompt: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃. How many moles of H₂ react with 2.0 mol of N₂?
cards.explain: 3 mol H₂ per 1 mol N₂: 2.0 × 3/1 = 6.0 mol. 0.67 mol divides by 3 instead of multiplying.

cards.prompt: A DNA template strand reads 3′-TAC-5′. Which codon does the ribosome read?
cards.explain: Transcription makes mRNA complementary to the template, with U in place of T: 3′-TAC-5′ gives 5′-AUG-3′. Ribosomes read mRNA, not DNA. ATG is the coding strand in DNA letters.

cards.prompt: Which molecule carries the codons that the ribosome reads?
cards.explain: mRNA carries the codons. tRNA carries the matching anticodons and brings the amino acids; DNA stays in the nucleus.

cards.prompt: The coding (non-template) strand is 5′-ATG GCT-3′. What is the mRNA?
cards.explain: mRNA has the same sequence as the coding strand, with U in place of T: 5′-AUG GCU-3′. UAC CGA is the complement, which is what the template strand would give if read as codons.

cards.prompt: The template strand is 3′-TAC AAA-5′. What is the second codon of the mRNA?
cards.explain: Template A pairs with U in RNA, so AAA gives the codon UUU (mRNA 5′-AUG UUU-3′). AAA is the template itself; TTT is the coding strand in DNA letters.
